To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
monadic queries can be learned interactively in polynomial time from partial annotations, which can be used for Web information extraction.

we developed new algorithms for interactive learning of node selecting queries in trees, and that we implemented them as a Web wrapper induction system that can extract information from Web pages with very few user interventions.

we have developed a novel formalism for monadic queries in trees, and we have implemented an interactive learning algorithm that is integrated into a visually interactive system for Web information extraction.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is the right class of queries for Web information extraction? How can these queries be learned efficiently? How can we make the process of wrapper induction interactive? We believe that our work provides answers to these questions.

the following contributions: (i) a new formalism for monadic queries in trees, (ii) new algorithms for learning these queries, (iii) new algorithms for interactive learning of these queries, (iv) an implementation of the algorithms in a Web browser, and (v) an experimental evaluation of the algorithms in realistic Web information extraction tasks.
the design of efficient algorithms that can learn monadic queries from annotated examples, which can be applied to visually interactive Web Information Extraction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our approach is the first one that provides a formal foundation of visually interactive Web information extractions systems, and is able to learn the most powerful class of queries for Web information extraction in polynomial time.

we provide a novel formal model of monadic queries in the form of NSTTs and pruning NSTTs, a new polynomial time interactive learning algorithm in the style of RPNI that learns monadic node selection tree queries from partial annotations, and an interactive Web information extraction prototype SQUIRREL, that is based on our new learning algorithm and that has been evaluated on realistic Web documents.
we have developed an effective and efficient interactive learning algorithm for learning monadic queries defined in MSO in trees, which can be used to extract information from unranked trees.

The main takeaway from our work is that
monadic queries can be learned interactively from partial annotations in polynomial time.
interactive learning can be a very powerful tool for Web information extraction and that it can be made very efficient by using the right representation of queries.
monadic node selection in unranked tree transducers is a promising formalism for Web information extraction.
